disease_label_per_paper: MSSA bacteremia with acute cervical transverse myelitis and C5-T1 osteomyelitis/perivertebral phlegmon
presentation_summary: 79-year-old man presented with 2 days of high-grade fever after acute upper back and neck pain 5 days earlier.
Initial neurologic examination showed left-arm weakness and ataxic broad-based gait; over 48 hours he developed flaccid tetraplegia, bilateral C3 sensory level, and respiratory failure.
Admission labs showed very high CRP and ESR with normal WBC count; two blood cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus.
Spinal MRI showed C3-C5 transverse myelitis and C5-T1 osteomyelitis with perivertebral phlegmon; TEE was negative for endocarditis.
